subject: torpedo ray
title: Roman Doctors Treated Headaches With This 220-Volt Fish

scenes.text: Roman doctors pressed this fish to your head. On purpose.
It's the torpedo ray, and the biggest kind can fire about 220 volts.
It hunts by wrapping its fins around a fish and shocking it still, then swallowing it whole.
About 2,000 years ago, a Roman physician wrote that a live one on the head eases headaches.
The shock left the painful spot numb. Its Latin name means numbness.
And the naval torpedo? It was named after this fish.

description:
The Atlantic torpedo ray can produce shocks of about 170-220 volts; it envelops prey with its pectoral fins, stuns it and swallows it whole.
Around 46 AD the Roman physician Scribonius Largus recommended a live torpedo ray against headaches and gout. The name comes from Latin torpere, to be numb, and the naval weapon was named after the fish.
Would you try the Roman cure?
first_comment: Electric rays are related to sharks. What's the strangest old medical cure you've heard of?
